# L1 converter

One session becomes one independent, single-episode Multi-Frequency LeRobot
dataset. The single-session entry requires the actual session directory, containing
`meta.json`, `videos/`, `timestamps/`, and `imu/` directly. An outer wrapper
directory fails before duration checks or conversion, with discovered session paths
in the error message. `--dry-run` applies the same path checks. Batch discovery
in `batch_convert.py` still supports flat and repeated nested session directories.

| Source camera | Output feature |
| --- | --- |
| left | observation.images.head_left |
| right | observation.images.head_right |
| bleft | observation.images.head_left_outer0 |
| bright | observation.images.head_right_outer0 |

Naming follows `docs/dataset_field_naming_rules.md`.

Each camera retains its own acquisition timestamps. All streams subtract one
shared Unix time origin, recorded in `meta/l1_source.json`. The left camera
defines the master index. Equal camera counts do not imply synchronized frames.
No padding, trimming, or timestamp rewriting is performed. Counts must agree
between the four cameras, metadata, timestamp files and decoded videos.
IMU retains its native timestamps and `[ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz]` sample order;
invalid source orientation quaternions are not exported as poses.

H264 MKV videos are losslessly remuxed into MP4 and decoded frame counts are
checked again. Video pixel statistics are not generated by this remux path.
Audio is saved directly as `audio/audio.wav`; audio logs are not copied.
Original metadata, task configs, timestamp files and calibration backups are
not copied. Audio has no established synchronization offset and is an attachment,
not an aligned dataset feature. Canonical calibration parameters are under
`calibrations/`, with explicit references for chained extrinsics. A minimal
conversion record in `meta/l1_source.json` supports resume and records the
shared time origin; it does not embed the original metadata.
Calibration time offsets are preserved,
not automatically applied to sensor timestamps.

## Requirements

Use the project's LeRobot environment (`requirements.txt`), plus PyYAML.
Both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` must be on PATH, or supplied with `--ffmpeg` and
`--ffprobe`. Dry-run only uses Python's standard library; it validates metadata,
timestamp files and IMU but does not inspect video contents or calibration YAML.

From the repository root:

```powershell
python format_convert/L1/batch_convert.py --source "C:/Users/22563/Desktop/data/L1/batch_0000001" --out "C:/Users/22563/Desktop/data/L1_lerobot/batch_0000001" --dry-run

python format_convert/L1/batch_convert.py --source "C:/Users/22563/Desktop/data/L1/batch_0000001" --out "C:/Users/22563/Desktop/data/L1_lerobot/batch_0000001" --workers 2
```

Single session (an outer directory containing exactly one session also works):

```bash
python format_convert/L1/convert_l1.py /path/to/session --out /path/to/output/session
```

Batch logs and statuses are stored in `_batch_logs/` and `_batch_status/`.
Rerunning skips complete outputs with matching source provenance. Existing
incomplete output directories are never overwritten. Conversion writes into a
unique adjacent `.partial-*` directory and publishes only after all steps
succeed. Failed staging directories remain available for inspection. Original
input files are never modified. Source and output trees must be disjoint.
